passage: Leila's phone buzzed during dinner, and the class group chat was full of laughing faces under a photo of her mid-sneeze, mouth wide open. Her cheeks burned. She typed "not funny!!" and deleted it, then typed something meaner and deleted that too. Her thumbs shook. Instead she took a screenshot and put the phone face down. Her older sister Elif saw her pushing peas around the plate. "What happened?" Elif asked. Leila showed her. Elif did not laugh. "Thank you for showing me. Tomorrow we take this to your teacher, and we keep the screenshot." Leila breathed out slowly. It still hurt, but it was no longer only hers to carry.

qa.q: What did Leila do with the photo instead of replying?
qa.a: She took a screenshot and put the phone face down.

qa.q: Why did Leila type messages and then delete them?
qa.a: She was hurt and angry and part of her wanted to snap back, but she seemed to sense that an angry reply would not help.

qa.q: What would you advise Leila to do with the screenshot?
qa.a: She should keep it safe and show it to her teacher with Elif's help, rather than answering the group in anger.

qa.q: How might Elif feel on seeing the photo?
qa.a: Elif was probably upset for her sister but stayed calm, since she did not laugh, thanked Leila for showing her and planned to go to the teacher.

grounding: A child is laughed at in a class chat, does not reply in anger, saves the screenshot and tells family and teacher.

passage:
I'm Harish, and I still remember the night the class group chat went off. Someone had posted a photo of me at sports day, falling face-first into the long-jump pit. Under it: laughing faces, one after another. "Sand monster lol."
My hands shook. I started typing something furious, then stopped. Instead I took screenshots, like my cousin had once told me, and went to Appa.
He read every message. "None of this is on you, and we can stop it." He saved the screenshots and messaged the class teacher that night. The photo was gone by morning.
Later, Anand messaged me privately: "I didn't laugh. That was mean." I read it three times.

qa.q: What was the photo in the class group chat?
qa.a: A photo of Harish falling face-first into the long-jump pit at sports day.

qa.q: How did Harish feel when the laughing faces kept appearing?
qa.a: Harish felt humiliated and angry, with shaking hands and the urge to type something furious.

qa.q: Why was saving screenshots and going to Appa a wise choice?
qa.a: It kept proof and brought in an adult, so the class teacher was told that night and the photo was removed by morning.

qa.q: How might Anand feel about what happened in the chat?
qa.a: Anand seems uncomfortable with the mocking and wants Harish to know not everyone laughed.

grounding: Classmates laugh at an embarrassing photo in the class group chat; the child does not reply in anger, saves screenshots and tells a parent, and it is stopped.

passage:
Note from the class teacher, Class 7, Tuesday.
This morning Gurleen came to me before assembly with her mother's phone. The night before, Ramesh had posted a photo of her asleep on the bus during the school trip, mouth open. Twenty classmates had reacted with laughing faces.
Gurleen's voice was steady, but her eyes were red. She said she had wanted to reply with something rude but had taken screenshots instead.
I told her she had done exactly the right thing and that none of this was her fault. I spoke to Ramesh and his parents at lunch. The photo was deleted and Ramesh apologised to Gurleen. I will talk to the whole class about the group chat tomorrow.

qa.q: How many classmates reacted with laughing faces?
How did Gurleen seem to feel when she came to the teacher?
qa.a: She seemed hurt and embarrassed, with red eyes, though she kept her voice steady.

qa.q: What did Gurleen do that helped stop the mockery?
qa.a: She didn't reply in anger; she took screenshots and brought them to the teacher, who acted that same day.

qa.q: How might Ramesh see the photo after talking to the teacher and his parents?
qa.a: Ramesh may now see that what felt like a joke was public humiliation for Gurleen, which is why he deleted it and apologised.

grounding: Classmates laugh at a photo of a girl in the group chat; she does not reply in anger, saves screenshots and tells a teacher, who stops it.
